def hackenbush_string_duel(strings, mover):
    """Blue-Red Hackenbush played on a set of vertical stalks.

    strings is a list of 1..12 strings (each of length 0..40, total length
    over all strings at most 200) over the alphabet {'B','R'}.  String i
    describes a stalk of edges planted on the ground: strings[i][0] is the
    bottom edge, strings[i][-1] the top edge.  'B' edges belong to Blue,
    'R' edges to Red.  mover is 'B' or 'R', the player who moves first.

    Players alternate turns.  On a turn, the player removes one edge of
    their own colour; every edge above it in the same stalk (all larger
    indices of that string) falls off and is removed too.  A player who
    has no edge of their colour anywhere loses.  Both play perfectly.

    Return a tuple (winner, i, j) where winner is 'B' or 'R', the player
    who wins under optimal play.  If winner == mover, (i, j) identifies a
    winning first move -- cut edge j of string i -- and among all winning
    first moves it is the lexicographically smallest pair (i, j).  If the
    first mover loses, return (winner, -1, -1).

    Edge cases: strings may be empty strings; if the first mover has no
    legal move at all they lose immediately.

    Note: with up to 12 stalks the reachable positions (one prefix length
    per stalk) can exceed 10**13, so any search over the joint game tree,
    memoised or not, is hopeless.

    >>> hackenbush_string_duel(["BBRR", "R"], "B")
    ('B', 0, 1)
    >>> hackenbush_string_duel(["BR", "RB"], "B")
    ('R', -1, -1)
    >>> hackenbush_string_duel(["RRB"], "R")
    ('R', 0, 0)
    """
